balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Evolution Mining Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Evolution Mining Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Evolution Mining Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Evolution Mining Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

goldProduction.title: Gold production and AISC
goldProduction.content:
Gold production is total group ounces sold/produced across all mines. AISC (all-in sustaining cost) is the industry-standard cost per ounce including sustaining capital -- the cost a mine must cover just to keep producing at the same rate.

For Evolution Mining: revenue is a function of ounces × realised gold price, and margin is a function of the gap between AISC and that price -- AISC has risen from A$907/oz in FY2017 to A$1,717/oz in FY2026 while production has been roughly flat, so almost all of the margin story is on the cost side, not the volume side.

What to watch:

  • AISC growth outpacing inflation (labour, diesel, royalties)
  • Production guidance beats/misses by mine
  • Whether copper by-product credits are lowering headline AISC

goldPrice.title: Gold price achieved vs production
goldPrice.content:
Gold price achieved is EVN's own realised average sale price per ounce (may differ from spot due to timing, hedging or provisional pricing), shown against total ounces produced.

For Evolution Mining: the achieved price has nearly quadrupled since FY2016 (A$1,597/oz to A$6,023/oz in FY2026) while production has barely moved -- almost all of the revenue growth on the chart above is price, not volume, which is the key risk if gold gives back its recent run.

What to watch:

  • Achieved price tracking spot AUD gold, not lagging or leading it materially
  • Production held flat or declining while price does the work
  • Any hedge book that caps upside in a rising market

copperProduction.title: Copper production
copperProduction.content:
Copper production (tonnes) is EVN's by-product credit, mainly from Ernest Henry and Cowal, which is netted against gold costs to lower reported AISC.

For Evolution Mining: copper output has grown roughly 4x since FY2017 (15kt to 76kt at the FY2025 peak) as Ernest Henry ramped, making EVN increasingly a gold-copper miner rather than a pure gold play -- copper price swings now matter to the AISC line even though copper isn't the headline commodity.

What to watch:

  • Copper price moves flowing through to AISC via the by-product credit
  • Ernest Henry underground transition risk to copper volumes

mineProduction.title: Gold production by mine
mineProduction.content:
Group gold production broken out by operating mine: Cowal (NSW), Ernest Henry (Qld, gold-copper), Mungari (WA), Northparkes (NSW, gold-copper JV) and Red Lake (Canada).

For Evolution Mining: Cowal alone is roughly 40% of group ounces and is the asset to watch for a group-level miss; Red Lake is the turnaround story management talks up most on calls. Mine-level disclosure only goes back to FY2024 in the filings, so this chart is shorter than the others.

What to watch:

  • Cowal's underground transition and grade trend
  • Red Lake's path toward its targeted production/cost run-rate
  • Any single mine driving a group guidance change

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Evolution Mining Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
